strings.name: Tim Duncan
strings.summary: Tim Duncan anchored the San Antonio Spurs with post footwork, bank shots, defense and steady collaboration. He spent all 19 NBA seasons with the club, winning five championships, two regular-season MVP awards and three Finals MVP awards. After retiring in 2016, he briefly served as an assistant coach and attended his Hall of Fame induction in 2021, maintaining a low public profile thereafter.

strings.highlights.h1.title: A constant across five titles
strings.highlights.h1.text: Championships in 1999, 2003, 2005, 2007 and 2014 connected several generations of Spurs players.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Initially trained as a swimmer, then turned to basketball; studied and played at Wake Forest from 1993 to 1997.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Two-way play and leadership
strings.highlights.h2.text: Two regular-season MVPs, three Finals MVPs and 15 All-Star selections reflect his sustained offensive and defensive contribution.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Hall of Fame ceremony
strings.timeline.t1.text: Attended the induction of the Class of 2020, postponed by the pandemic until 2021.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Spurs assistant coach
strings.timeline.t2.text: Joined Gregg Popovich’s staff for the 2019–20 season, subsequently leaving the full-time coaching position.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Ended a 19-year NBA career
strings.timeline.t3.text: Announced retirement after spending his entire NBA career with one franchise.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Fifth championship
strings.timeline.t4.text: Joined Parker, Ginóbili and a younger generation of teammates in defeating Miami for the title.
strings.timeline.t5.title: MVP and a second title
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won his second consecutive regular-season MVP and led the Spurs to a championship, also earning Finals MVP.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First NBA championship
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won the title and Finals MVP in his second professional season.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First overall pick
strings.timeline.t7.text: Entered the NBA after four college seasons as the first draft pick and became Rookie of the Year the following season.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Formation at Wake Forest
strings.timeline.t8.text: Entered college and developed post skills and defense over four seasons, winning major national college player awards as a senior.
